entries.name: Searing Strike
entries.notes: SHIPPED — id, kind and element-variant expansion kept verbatim per naming.v1.json idNamespaces.affixFamilies (g.on-hit existingFamilies). `roles` is the on-hit column of ssot-affixes.md §4.3's role x group matrix, translated from the stale 12-role table to core.v1.json's 15 ids: sense-utility->sense, manipulator-offense->manipulator, jewel-major stays, jewel-minor->jewel-minor-a and jewel-minor-b, armament-primary/-secondary stay. The commander-only `standard` row carries weight 0 for on-hit and is correctly absent. Every entry in this file shares this identical roles list — the matrix has one row per role per GROUP, not per family. `nameWords.suffix` reuses the fire-variant words ssot-affixes.md §4.12 already shows as shipped ("of Sparks"/"of Cinders"/"of Embers"), applied across all seven element slots the same way elemental_power reuses one word set across variants (atom-family-library.md §3.2).

entries.name: Lifesteal
entries.displayTemplate: heal {value}% of damage dealt on hit
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id kept verbatim. No `element` param and no `variants` — ssot-affixes.md's own citations (`atom.lifesteal.t3`) show no variant segment. `nameWords.suffix` reuses the shipped words shown in ssot-affixes.md §4.12.

entries.name: Retribution
entries.displayTemplate: reflect {value}% of damage taken back at the attacker
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id kept verbatim. The only OnDamageTaken family in this group — it still belongs to g.on-hit per naming.v1.json and ssot-affixes.md §4.1, since the group is about the wearer's hit exchange, not exclusively the wearer's own swing. No shipped word table exists for it in ssot-affixes.md's illustrative sample, so `nameWords` is minted here, following the same suffix `of-construct` grammar as the shown examples.

entries.name: Volley
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% chance to fire an additional bullet on hit
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id kept verbatim. `kindId: spawn.entity` with `params.kind: "bullet"` matches AtomKindRegistry's spawn.entity schema, whose `x`/`hp`/`maxHp` params are honoured only for `kind=bullet|zombie` — this family supplies none of those since the spawned bullet inherits the wearer's own attack, per atom-family-library.md §3.5's sketch ("on-hit extra bullet"). `powerBand: low` keeps a multiplicative extra-attack rider modest relative to the additive riders above it, the same relative-pull judgement the exemplar makes between sibling families.

entries.name: Vengeful Mending
entries.displayTemplate: heal {value}% of damage taken on hit
entries.notes: NEW family minted on this group's reserved `hit` stem (naming.v1.json idNamespaces.affixFamilies), word `mend` — short and mechanical, not a flavour word. Fills the one on-hit combination the four shipped families leave open: `resource.delta` + `OnDamageTaken` + heal, the defensive mirror of `lifesteal` (which heals on the trigger the wearer causes, not the trigger the wearer suffers) and distinct from `retribution` (which reflects damage on the same trigger rather than healing).

entries.name: Retaliatory Shot
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% chance to fire a bullet back at the attacker when hit
entries.notes: NEW family, stem `hit`, word `retort` (a sharp reply — mechanical, not a theme adjective). `volley` fires its extra bullet on the wearer's own hit; this fires the same shaped bullet on the OPPOSITE trigger, when the wearer is struck — a genuinely different combination from every shipped family in the group.

entries.name: Follow-Through Strike
entries.notes: NEW family, stem `hit`, word `followthrough`. A plain, non-elemental bonus-damage rider on the same trigger as `searing_strike`, deliberately carrying no `element` param and no `variants` block so it is a single-row family rather than a seven-slot one — the un-typed sibling next to the elemental family, the way `might` (flat) sits next to `elemental_power` (typed) in the prefix side. `powerBand: low` keeps it from outclassing the elemental rider it sits beside.
